data.reason: Using one of the two blind raters is a documented choice among the crowdsourced teams; it discards information from the second rater but keeps the same exposure.
The mirror of the rater 1 choice: a single rater scale, with the caveat that this rater scored darker on average.
Contrasting clearly light with clearly dark players is a recognised sensitivity check, but it discards the middle of the scale and changes the sample.
Referees seen in few dyads give unstable rates, so requiring a minimum is a standard precision rule; the cut-off is a judgement.
Height, weight and position are pre-treatment player characteristics that relate to carding; adjusting for them is standard.
League country is a pre-treatment context variable; adjusting for it alongside physique is a common specification among the research teams.
Red cards are rare counts over varying exposure, so a Poisson model with a log-games offset is the textbook alternative to the binomial model.
A player appears in many dyads, so clustering the errors by player corrects the uncertainty without changing the estimand.

steps.title: Fit the model
steps.description: Estimate the odds ratio of a red card per game.

options.label: Binomial GLM
options.rationale: Red cards out of games is a binomial outcome.
options.spec: GLM Binomial on (redCards, games - redCards); OR = exp(coef).
options.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm


def estimate(df, ctx):
    covariates = list(ctx.get("covariates", []))
    needed = ["skin_tone", "games", "redCards", "playerShort"] + covariates
    data = df.dropna(subset=needed).copy()
    data["playerShort"] = data["playerShort"].astype(str)
    numeric = [c for c in covariates if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    categorical = [c for c in covariates if c not in numeric]
    parts = [data[["skin_tone"]].astype(float), data[numeric].astype(float)]
    if categorical:
        parts.append(
            pd.get_dummies(data[categorical].astype(str), drop_first=True, dtype=float)
        )
    exog = sm.add_constant(pd.concat(parts, axis=1), has_constant="add")
    successes = data["redCards"].clip(upper=data["games"]).astype(float)
    endog = pd.concat([successes, data["games"].astype(float) - successes], axis=1)
    fit = sm.GLM(endog, exog, family=sm.families.Binomial()).fit()
    low, high = fit.conf_int().loc["skin_tone"]
    return {
        "estimate": float(np.exp(fit.params["skin_tone"])),
        "ci_low": float(np.exp(low)),
        "ci_high": float(np.exp(high)),
        "p_value": float(fit.pvalues["skin_tone"]),
        "n": int(len(data)),
        "extra": {"log_odds": float(fit.params["skin_tone"])},
    }

options.rationale: Red cards are rare counts over exposure.
options.spec: GLM Poisson with offset log(games); reports the rate ratio.
options.code:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm


def estimate(df, ctx):
    covariates = list(ctx.get("covariates", []))
    needed = ["skin_tone", "games", "redCards", "playerShort"] + covariates
    data = df.dropna(subset=needed).copy()
    data["playerShort"] = data["playerShort"].astype(str)
    numeric = [c for c in covariates if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    categorical = [c for c in covariates if c not in numeric]
    parts = [data[["skin_tone"]].astype(float), data[numeric].astype(float)]
    if categorical:
        parts.append(
            pd.get_dummies(data[categorical].astype(str), drop_first=True, dtype=float)
        )
    exog = sm.add_constant(pd.concat(parts, axis=1), has_constant="add")
    offset = np.log(data["games"].astype(float))
    fit = sm.GLM(
        data["redCards"].astype(float), exog, family=sm.families.Poisson(), offset=offset
    ).fit()
    low, high = fit.conf_int().loc["skin_tone"]
    return {
        "estimate": float(np.exp(fit.params["skin_tone"])),
        "ci_low": float(np.exp(low)),
        "ci_high": float(np.exp(high)),
        "p_value": float(fit.pvalues["skin_tone"]),
        "n": int(len(data)),
        "extra": {"log_rate_ratio": float(fit.params["skin_tone"])},
    }

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm


def estimate(df, ctx):
    covariates = list(ctx.get("covariates", []))
    needed = ["skin_tone", "games", "redCards", "playerShort"] + covariates
    data = df.dropna(subset=needed).copy()
    data["playerShort"] = data["playerShort"].astype(str)
    numeric = [c for c in covariates if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    categorical = [c for c in covariates if c not in numeric]
    parts = [data[["skin_tone"]].astype(float), data[numeric].astype(float)]
    if categorical:
        parts.append(
            pd.get_dummies(data[categorical].astype(str), drop_first=True, dtype=float)
        )
    exog = sm.add_constant(pd.concat(parts, axis=1), has_constant="add")
    successes = data["redCards"].clip(upper=data["games"]).astype(float)
    endog = pd.concat([successes, data["games"].astype(float) - successes], axis=1)
    groups = pd.factorize(data["playerShort"])[0]
    fit = sm.GLM(endog, exog, family=sm.families.Binomial()).fit(
        cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": groups}
    )
    low, high = fit.conf_int().loc["skin_tone"]
    return {
        "estimate": float(np.exp(fit.params["skin_tone"])),
        "ci_low": float(np.exp(low)),
        "ci_high": float(np.exp(high)),
        "p_value": float(fit.pvalues["skin_tone"]),
        "n": int(len(data)),
        "extra": {"log_odds": float(fit.params["skin_tone"])},
    }

option.label: Full set plus referee-country bias scores
option.rationale: Referee-country implicit and explicit bias could confound who is carded; several teams in the published study adjusted for them.
option.spec: covariates = [position, leagueCountry, height, weight, meanIAT, meanExp].
option.source: Silberzahn et al. (2018), Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science

option.label: Only referees from low implicit-bias countries
option.rationale: Cleaner comparison among referees with less measured bias.
option.spec: Drop unrated rows, keep referees whose country meanIAT is below median.

data.reason: Adjusting for referee-country bias scores is a standard confounder control, keeps the population and the estimand unchanged, and was used by published analysts.
Keeping only low-bias referees changes the population and tests the question where bias is least likely, so a null there says nothing about referees in general.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import statsmodels.api as sm


def estimate(df, ctx):
    covariates = list(ctx.get("covariates", []))
    needed = ["skin_tone", "games", "redCards", "playerShort"] + covariates
    data = df.dropna(subset=needed).copy()
    data["playerShort"] = data["playerShort"].astype(str)
    numeric = [c for c in covariates if pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(data[c])]
    categorical = [c for c in covariates if c not in numeric]
    parts = [data[["skin_tone"]].astype(float), data[numeric].astype(float)]
    if categorical:
        parts.append(
            pd.get_dummies(data[categorical].astype(str), drop_first=True, dtype=float)
        )
    exog = sm.add_constant(pd.concat(parts, axis=1), has_constant="add")
    successes = data["redCards"].clip(upper=data["games"]).astype(float)
    endog = pd.concat([successes, data["games"].astype(float) - successes], axis=1)
    groups = pd.factorize(data["playerShort"])[0]
    fit = sm.GLM(endog, exog, family=sm.families.Binomial()).fit(
        cov_type="cluster", cov_kwds={"groups": groups}
    )
    low, high = fit.conf_int().loc["skin_tone"]
    return {
        "estimate": float(np.exp(fit.params["skin_tone"])),
        "ci_low": float(np.exp(low)),
        "ci_high": float(np.exp(high)),
        "p_value": float(fit.pvalues["skin_tone"]),
        "n": int(len(data)),
        "extra": {"log_odds": float(fit.params["skin_tone"])},
    }

report.narrative: With the default choices dark-skinned players are carded more: OR 1.34 (95% CI 1.13 to 1.58), p = 0.0006, n = 124,621 dyads, so the verdict is BIAS DETECTED. The minimal flip changes Measure skin tone from "Mean of both raters" to "Rater 2 only" and Choose which dyads to keep from "Rated players only" to "Rated players, referees with 22+ dyads" and Adjust for context from "No covariates" to "Physique plus league country". None of the 9 single-decision changes reverses it: the odds ratio stays between 1.27 and 1.36 and every interval keeps excluding 1. None of the 10 pairs ranked most likely to flip it does either. The verdict first changes at three simultaneous changes: 4 such universes reach NO CLEAR EVIDENCE, with odds ratios of 1.20 to 1.25 and p between 0.055 and 0.069. All of them adjust for the full covariate set, and most add player-clustered errors and the second rater alone. The minimal flip (second rater only, referees with 22 or more dyads, full covariates; OR 1.20 (95% CI 1.00 to 1.46), p = 0.055) was re-executed from a fresh sandbox and reproduced exactly. Across all defensible universes the odds ratio runs from 1.20 to 1.36, inside the human teams' range of 0.89 to 2.93. The only one-decision change that did flip the verdict, keeping low-bias referees only (OR 1.25 (95% CI 0.99 to 1.59), p = 0.066), was rejected as an indefensible change of population.
caveats: Robustness headline is design-weighted (90%): uniform random sample of the grid: 12 draws (each decision picks each of its options equally), 10 distinct results; independent of the beam search. The share among the explored universes is 87%, but the beam search samples the universes that are closest to flipping, so that figure leans toward flips.

The minimal flip changes the covariates of the model (adds 16 unnamed columns): adjusted versus unadjusted answers a different question, so this is an estimand change, not a re-analysis of the same quantity.
Odds ratios compare the lightest with the darkest tone on a 0 to 1 scale and rest on player-referee dyads, not on individual refereeing decisions.
The estimate is an association; it cannot separate bias from unmeasured differences in playing style or match context.
Influence is measured under fixed defaults and is not a causal statement about the world.
